FIX-DRS-CLAIM-TRUSTS-CACHED-DISPATCH-LANE-NOT-EFFECTIVE-NEXT-AGENT (backlog, P1) is scoped entirely to the STALE-VALUE failure: both its evidence occurrences (FIX-CHEF-BIZCTX 2026-08-14T02:21Z, UC-CDC-P1 22:35Z) are rows whose dispatch_lane pointed at the WRONG agent, and its AC's regression fixture tests exactly that ("a row whose dispatch_lane predates a later next_agent change claims to the LATER agent").

There is a second, more severe failure mode on the same line that the row does not name and that fixture does not cover: dispatch_lane == NULL.

MECHANISM (read at source, not inferred):
- scripts/devteam-backlog-claim-design-router-sweep.jq:73-81 selects $swept[0] — the FIRST DRS-stamped row in ready[] ARRAY ORDER, with no priority sort — then binds ($picked.dispatch_lane) as $lane with no null-guard, and writes head.next_agent = $lane verbatim.
- A null $lane yields head.status=in_progress with head.next_agent=null. The router cannot spawn a null agent type (CLAUDE.md forbids guessing one), so the row sits claimed in in_progress[] at status IN_PROGRESS, consuming a wip_in_progress slot. That alone fails BOUNDED-1's WIP<1 gate. Unlike the SLS variant this does NOT regenerate — the row has left ready[], so DRS will not re-pick it — it strands ONCE, permanently, until hand-corrected.
- The flow doc asserts this cannot happen: main.md § DRS states the promote script "Resolves dispatch_lane = effective_next_agent($detail_items) directly (no owner-fallback needed — every DRS candidate already has a present, non-empty, non-dev, allowlisted next_agent by construction)". That premise holds only for rows promoted by the CURRENT promote script. It is false for rows promoted before dispatch_lane stamping existed, and nothing re-validates on the way through.

LIVE TRIGGER, dated:
docs/data/orch/orch-state.json .task_board.ready[] currently holds 3 DRS-stamped rows, in this array order:
  [0] UC-SDF-P6                                              lane=ba
  [1] FIX-COWORK-PUBLISHED-MARKER-TTL-28H-EXCEEDS-24H-DAILY-CADENCE  lane=NULL  priority=P0  promoted_at=2026-08-14T22:35:15Z
  [2] UC-SDF-P2                                              lane=ba
Promote appends to the end of ready[], so index [1] is stable. DRS gets one turn per 6-lane rotation (~1 per 3h at the 7,37 cadence). Next DRS turn claims [0]; the turn after that claims the null-lane P0. Estimated strand window: ~2026-08-23T23:00Z, +/- one rotation.

Note this is a P0 row, and it is the same row that agents-architect correctly lane-moved out of in_progress[] on 2026-08-23T14:07Z — it would be re-stranded by a script, not by an agent's judgment.

REQUESTED, in preference order:
1. Widen the existing row rather than minting a duplicate — add the null case to its AC and require the regression fixture to cover BOTH shapes (stale-non-null AND null). The AC as written ("NEVER reads a persisted dispatch_lane value") already implies the null fix, but an implementer satisfying only the named fixture could ship a "use dispatch_lane if present, else re-resolve" shortcut that still leaves null unhandled.
2. Consider stamping dispatch_lane onto FIX-COWORK-PUBLISHED-MARKER-TTL-28H-EXCEEDS-24H-DAILY-CADENCE now via orch-apply.sh, using the same resolver the FALLBACK branch already uses (resolved_dispatch_lane($detail_items) -> effective_next_agent, else effective_owner, else "developer"), to defuse the trigger ahead of the fix landing. Not done here: the router does dispatch bookkeeping only, and picking a lane for a P0 row is a content decision.

Also worth folding in: the identical no-null-guard pattern is documented on the SLS PRIMARY claim path (feedback_sls_primary_claim_null_dispatch_lane_yields_unspawnable_head.md, hit live 2026-08-23T12:56Z on FIX-AUDITOR-C04-PARSEDAT-RECENCY-PREDICATE). Two claim scripts, same defect, separate rows — a shared null-guard helper in scripts/lib/devteam-eligibility.jq would close both.

Emitted by the router during dev-team tick cron:dev-team:2026-08-23T16:37Z, rotation SELECTED=drs. Detection was incidental: the null was visible only because the swept-set listing was read before running the claim. Nothing mechanised would have surfaced it.
